query: A tank holds 1200 litres and drains at 15 litres per minute while a pump refills it at 4 litres per minute; how long until it is empty? Show the reasoning.

scene.title: Tank drainage time calculation
scene.subtitle: Calculating net flow rate and time to empty

answer.headline: It takes approximately 109.09 minutes, or 1 hour and 49 minutes, for the tank to empty completely.
body: The net rate at which water leaves the tank is the difference between the rate of drainage and the rate of the pump. Since water is draining at 15 litres per minute and being added at 4 litres per minute, the tank loses a net volume of 11 litres every minute.

To determine how long it takes for the tank to empty, we divide the total capacity of 1200 litres by the net loss rate of 11 litres per minute. This calculation results in approximately 109.09 minutes, indicating that the system will reach zero volume in just under two hours.
caveats: Assumes flow rates remain constant until the tank is empty.
Assumes the tank is full at the start of the process.

items.label: Calculate time to empty
items.detail: Divide the total capacity of 1200 litres by the net depletion rate of 11 litres per minute.

items.label: Convert to human time
items.detail: 109.09 minutes is equivalent to 1 hour (60 minutes) plus 49.09 minutes.

items.label: R_net = R_out - R_in
items.detail: The net rate of change is the difference between outflows and inflows.

items.label: t = C / R_net
items.detail: Time required to drain a container of capacity C at a net rate of R_net.
